lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Paraphrase without copying: "Heat from the sun can cause evaporation from a puddle."

FEEDBACK
Own words + source tag; keep meaning true.

CHECK
Changing a few words but keeping the sentence skeleton can still be too close.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Create three quotes and three paraphrases with attribution for your project. Mark which is which.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Create three quotes and three paraphrases with attribution for your project. Mark which is which. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using paraphrase on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Changing a few words but keeping the sentence skeleton can still be too close.. Correction: Own words + source tag; keep meaning true.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Changing a few words but keeping the sentence skeleton can still be too close. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating paraphrase on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with paraphrase, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about paraphrase with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for paraphrase. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Quote: According to the museum kids page, "…" Paraphrase: The page explains that… with a source tag. Never invent a source name.

TRY FIRST
Paraphrase without copying: "Heat from the sun can cause evaporation from a puddle."

FEEDBACK
Own words + source tag; keep meaning true.
teach_steps.explain:
Paraphrasing puts ideas in your words; quoting keeps exact words in marks—both need attribution so research stays honest.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Changing a few words but keeping the sentence skeleton can still be too close. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
